messages:
maya (sec-eng): alert -> unusual secret access from exporter-sa in analytics-temp. triggered by our anomaly detector.

maya (sec-eng): quick log snippet:
```
2026-03-20T08:12:03Z kube-apiserver audit: user=system:serviceaccount:analytics-temp:exporter-sa verb=get resource=secrets name=prod-db-creds
2026-03-20T08:12:04Z iam: ClusterRoleBinding created by deployer-service deploy/ci-pipeline
```

dave (oncall): copied. is this read-only or exfil attempt? any data transfer logs?

maya (sec-eng): we see repeated GETs from that SA to multiple secrets across namespaces. traffic egress is small but suspicious. no big data dump yet.

tony (infra): if ClusterRoleBinding was created by CI, we need to revoke immediately. i can remove the binding now. agree revoke first, investigate after.

maya (sec-eng): yes revoke. also freeze tokens for exporter-sa and rotate any KMS keys referenced by those secrets.

leo (platform): im on it — removing binding:
```
kubectl delete clusterrolebinding ci-deployer-temp-bridge
kubectl auth can-i --as=system:serviceaccount:analytics-temp:exporter-sa get secrets --all-namespaces
```

leo (platform): done — binding removed at 08:16Z. can-i now returns forbidden. :white_check_mark:

olivia (devex): CI pipeline change that created the binding: last rollout at 08:09Z. i'll revert the pipeline step and open PR to remove cluster-admin creation logic.

maya (sec-eng): please also add immediate deny rule in authz controller for that SA as defense-in-depth.

tony (infra): putting a deny rule now on authz-policy svc:
```
apiVersion: authz.redwood/v1
kind: DenyPolicy
subjects:
  - kind: ServiceAccount
    name: exporter-sa
    namespace: analytics-temp
rules:
  - verbs: ["*"]
    resources: ["secrets"]
```

tony (infra): deny policy pushed at 08:20Z.

maya (sec-eng): nice. next: collect audit logs, CI audit trail, and KMS access logs. sec-bot, can you aggregate and post to the thread? @sec-bot

sec-bot: collecting logs from kube-apiserver, cloud KMS, and CI logs. ETA 6m.

sec-bot: uploaded artifacts to /secure/incidents/2367894321/log_bundle.tar.gz

dave (oncall): good. assigning owners: maya for sec triage, tony for infra fix/rollback, olivia for CI fix, leo for short-term containment.

olivia (devex): opened PR 4682 to remove cluster role creation and added tests to prevent SA->clusterrole in pipelines. linking: https://git.redwood/olivia/pulls/4682

maya (sec-eng): forensics note: possible cause is an allowlist expansion in role-mapper that treated namespace pattern 'analytics-*' as wildcard across org. need config rollback and postmortem.

maya (sec-eng): do we have evidence of secrets read outside analytics-temp? logs show reads in 'billing' and 'ml-workbench' as well.

leo (platform): yes found three namespaces touched. we'll run a quick scan to list secrets accessed by that SA:
```
kubectl get events --field-selector involvedObject.name=exporter-sa --all-namespaces | grep secret
```

tony (infra): KMS logs show decrypt calls for the secret blobs at 08:12-08:18Z from exporter-sa's service key. marking those keys for rotation now.

maya (sec-eng): rotate keys, revoke SA tokens, and snapshot audit logs. also notify compliance — possible PII exposure.

dave (oncall): compliance pinged. legal wants timeline and list of secrets accessed. maya, olivia, can you draft initial incident note?

olivia (devex): drafting and will attach logs from sec-bot bundle.

sec-bot: note: CI system account that created the binding is 'deployer-ci', token issued from ephemeral runner. we should rotate runner creds.

maya (sec-eng): longer term actions: (1) remove pattern-based allowlists that expand to cluster-level, (2) add pre-merge linting to CI that detects clusterrole/clusterrolebinding creation, (3) enable realtime audit alert for cross-namespace secret access, (4) update incident runbook with this flow.

dave (oncall): agreed. timeline: revoke at 08:16, deny pushed 08:20, keys rotation started 08:22, logs uploaded 08:26. next check-in in 1h unless more findings.

maya (sec-eng): closing immediate responder loop. keeping thread open for forensics. thanks all. :thumbsup:
